r0068: 37.  The applicant complained that an administrative body had been able to delay the enforcement of a final judicial decision.
r0069: 38.  The Government considered that the right of access to a court had not been infringed in the present case, since the applicant had been able to apply first to the magistrate (*juge d’instance*), who had granted his application and ordered that the premises be vacated, and could subsequently have applied to the regional administrative court (*tribunal administratif régional*) to challenge the refusal to grant him police assistance.
r0070: 39.  The Court reiterates that in Italian cases likewise concerning delays in the eviction of tenants, it examined the complaints concerning the length of the eviction proceedings from the more general standpoint of the right to a court, and concluded that the applicants had not enjoyed the right of access to a court (see Immobiliare Saffi, cited above, § 61, and Edoardo Palumbo v. Italy, no. 15919/89, § 42-45).
r0071: 40.  Those were cases in which the enforcement of the order for possession had been excessively delayed as a result of the Prefect’s refusal to grant police assistance. The Court had observed in particular that, from the moment when the Prefect became the authority with power to set the date of the enforced eviction, and in view of the absence of effective judicial review of his decisions, the owners had been deprived of their right to have their dispute with their tenants decided by a court, as required by Article 6 of the Convention.
r0072: 41.  The Court considers that the present case differs from the above-mentioned cases. In the present case, on 14 December 1991 the applicant applied to the enforcement judge (*juge de l’exécution*) for a ruling that his tenant, being in arrears with the rent, could not benefit from the suspension of the provision of police assistance. That judge examined the matter and subsequently granted the application on 17 April 1993 (see paragraph 17 above). Shortly afterwards, on 2 July 1993, the applicant obtained police assistance (see paragraph 20 above).
r0073: 42.  In those circumstances, the Court considers that the applicant enjoyed his right of access to a court. It remains to be examined whether the applicant enjoyed his right to a court, of which the right to the enforcement of a judgment or decision given by any court forms an integral part (see, mutatis mutandis, Hornsby v. Greece, judgment of 19 March 1997, Reports of Judgments and Decisions 1997-II, p. 510, § 40).
r0074: 43.  The Court reiterates in this connection that the execution of a judicial decision cannot be prevented, invalidated or unduly delayed (see Immobiliare Saffi, cited above, § 74).
r0075: 44.  In the present case, the applicant obtained an order for possession on 9 October 1987 (see paragraph above), which was not enforced until 2 July 1993, that is, approximately four years after the applicant had served notice on the tenant, on 3 August 1989, requiring her to vacate the premises, thereby initiating the enforcement proceedings (see paragraph 14 above). The Court emphasises in this connection that the applicant was entitled to obtain police assistance as a matter of priority, since the tenant was in arrears with the rent; approximately sixteen months nevertheless passed before that priority was recognised by the magistrate (*juge d’instance*) (see paragraph 17 above).
r0076: 45.  The Court considers that the Government have not shown that this stay of execution lasted only for such period as was strictly necessary to enable a satisfactory solution to be found to the public-order problems facing the Italian authorities; in particular, the Court notes that the Government, who submitted that the tenant had a dependent child and a modest income, have not shown that during those four years the authorities sought a solution to her housing problems (see, mutatis mutandis, A.O. v. Italy, no. 22534/93, § 29).
r0077: 46.  In those circumstances, the Court considers that there has been a violation of the right to a court guaranteed by Article 6 § 1 of the Convention. The complaint concerning the length of the proceedings must be regarded as having been absorbed by the foregoing complaint.
